x_posts.text:

First champ to start 0-2 in 15 years. The Knicks have a problem. #NewYorkKnicks

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:

He scored 7 of his 36 in the final 80 seconds to put away the defending champs.

Not a slump. Not a slow start. Tatum is operating at a different level. #Celtics

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

The defending champions are 0-2, and the NBA world is paying attention.

Boston defeated New York 107-103 at TD Garden on Friday night, and it wasn't particularly close down the stretch. Jayson Tatum put the game away with seven late points in the final 80 seconds — 36 total, 9 rebounds, 7 assists in a complete, suffocating performance.

For the Knicks, the story is bigger than one game, or even two. New York has now become the first defending NBA champion to start the season 0-2 in 15 years. The championship banner still hangs at Madison Square Garden. But the team that earned it is two losses in and looking for answers.

Karl-Anthony Towns did what he could with 22 points. Jalen Brunson, the heartbeat of this team's title run, was limited to 19 on a rough 7-for-19 shooting night. The margin has been slim in both losses — but slim margins going the wrong way have a way of becoming a pattern.

The question isn't whether New York will recover. They will. They're too talented not to. The question is whether this slow start reveals something structural — a team that hasn't yet found its regular season intensity after a long championship run.

Paul George and the Celtics are 1-1 and playing with confidence. For New York, the next week will say everything about what kind of team they'll be this season.

article.headline: Knicks Go 0-2: Tatum's 36 Points Send Defending Champions Into Early Crisis

stories.title: Rockets 114, Spurs 110 — Amen Thompson Seals It

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
The Spurs tied it at 96. The Rockets had a problem.

Then Amen Thompson blocked what could have been the go-ahead shot and Houston closed it out.

Rockets 114, Spurs 110. Defense wins games. #Rockets

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM ET

Last night in San Antonio, the Houston Rockets looked like a team that might be in trouble.

The Spurs, playing with serious early-season energy, clawed back into the game and tied it at 96 late in the fourth quarter. One missed shot, one turnover — and a Rockets team trying to protect a home-court advantage had a real problem on its hands.

Then Amen Thompson made the play of the night.

Thompson timed a game-saving block perfectly at the right moment, swatting away what could have been a go-ahead shot and essentially ending San Antonio's comeback. Houston closed it out, 114-110, and escaped with a win they'll want to build on.

The Rockets aren't flashy. They aren't scoring 130 points and making highlight reels every night. But they're competing, they're making plays when it counts, and Amen Thompson's defensive instincts — always his calling card — showed up exactly when Houston needed them.

Three games into the season, that's the kind of win that builds confidence.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 11:00 AM ET

The Atlanta Hawks didn't just beat Charlotte last night. They set a franchise record.

128-81. A 47-point margin of victory that has never been matched in franchise history. The Hornets were overmatched, overwhelmed, and outscored from wire to wire in what became a statement performance for an Atlanta team that looks genuinely dangerous this season.

Jalen Johnson was the engine with 19 points, 8 assists, and 7 rebounds — the kind of efficient, multidimensional stat line that underscores why he's an emerging star in this league. The Hawks played with pace, with joy, and with the kind of precision that blowouts rarely capture.

For Charlotte, it's a brutal start. Naz Reid led the Hornets with 17 points, but this wasn't a game where individual performances mattered much. The Hornets are finding out quickly that there's a wide gap between where they are and where the Eastern Conference's better teams are operating.

For Atlanta, this is a signal to the rest of the East. The Hawks are here, they're deep, and they're playing their best basketball in years.

stories.title: Lakers 125, Clippers 117 — Reaves and Kessler Lead LA Derby Win

x_posts.label: Post 4

Austin Reaves: 28 pts, 9 ast.

The Lakers won the LA Derby 125-117 and neither stat line is from their biggest star.

That's a deep team. #LakeShow

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM ET

The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Clippers 125-117 Friday night, and the story isn't just the win. It's who made the biggest plays.

Austin Reaves finished with 28 points and 9 assists — a performance that once again underscores why he's one of the most valuable two-way players in the Western Conference. He created shots for others, hit big buckets under pressure, and ran the offense with the kind of composure you typically see from franchise veterans.

But the most surprising performance of the LA Derby came from Walker Kessler, who posted 22 points and 6 blocks in a dominant showing at center. Kessler's combination of rim protection and offensive efficiency made him impossible to handle, and the Clippers had no answers for his activity in the paint.

For a Lakers team that enters this season with high expectations, the message from the first two games is clear: this isn't a team built around one star. It's a roster with multiple contributors who can take over a game, and the depth makes them genuinely dangerous in the West.

Bucks at 76ers, 7:30 PM ET. Eight games tonight across the NBA.

What are you watching? #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:30 PM ET

Eight games. One headliner.

Tonight the Milwaukee Bucks visit the Philadelphia 76ers at the Wells Fargo Center, and Giannis Antetokounmpo against LeBron James in the same game for the first time in 2026-27 is exactly the kind of appointment television this league is built around.

Neither team has had a perfect start. The Sixers are rolling at 2-0 following their incredible comeback over Cleveland and their solid home opener. Milwaukee, like the rest of the league, is still finding its footing. Tonight is an early measuring stick for both franchises.

Beyond the 76ers game, there's plenty to watch:
- **Spurs at Mavericks** (8:00 PM ET) — San Antonio tries to bounce back after last night's loss
- **Rockets at Hawks** (8:30 PM ET) — Back-to-back for Houston, and Atlanta just set a franchise blowout record
- **Warriors at Suns** (10:00 PM ET) — Western Conference matchup in Phoenix to close out the night

It's early October, and the NBA already has drama, rivalries, and star power delivering every night.
